events.label: birth
events.text: Born in Delhi to educationist S. K. Rudra and Priyobala Singha.

evidence.quote: 20 October 1896

events.text: Selected for OTC at Inns of Court; could not complete it as the war ended.

evidence.quote: In 1918 , he was selected for OTC at Inns of court

events.text: Joined first batch of Kings Commissioned Indian Officers at Daly College, Indore.

evidence.quote: In 1919 , he joined the first batch of the Kings Commissioned Indian Officers

events.text: Commissioned into 28th Punjabis as temporary second lieutenant.

evidence.quote: On 1 December 1919 , Rudra was commissioned into the 28th Punjabis as a temporary second lieutenant

events.text: Appointed to permanent commission as second lieutenant.

evidence.quote: on 17 July 1920 , he was appointed to a permanent commission as a second lieutenant
Promoted to temporary lieutenant on 1 December 1920
July 1921
receiving promotion to the substantive rank of lieutenant
Rudra was promoted to captain on 17 October 1927
he was promoted to major on 27 March 1939

events.label: campaign
events.text: Took part in the Arakan Campaign, lasting to 1943.

evidence.quote: he took part in the Arakan Campaign 1942–43

events.text: Transferred to the General Staff at GHQ India by General Claude Auchinleck.

evidence.quote: In 1943 , Lieutenant Colonel Rudra was transferred to the General Staff at GHQ India
promoted to acting lieutenant-colonel on 15 June 1943
to temporary lieutenant-colonel on 14 September 1943
promoted to acting colonel on 3 April 1945
temporary colonel on 3 October 1945
acting brigadier on 27 March 1946

events.label: honour
events.text: Appointed Officer of the Order of the British Empire (Military Division) in Birthday Honours.

evidence.quote: In June 1946 , Rudra was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire
The following month , on 17 July 1946
he was promoted to the substantive rank of lieutenant-colonel

events.text: Served as Military Secretary at GHQ; instrumental in forming the post-independence Indian Army.

evidence.quote: In 1948 , the year after India gained its independence , Brigadier Rudra was serving as the Military Secretary at GHQ
with promotion to substantive major-general on 1 January 1950

events.text: Retired from the Indian Army after commanding Southern Command.

evidence.quote: and retired in 1959
3 November 1993

undated_mentions: Educated at St Stephen's College, Delhi
Educated at Trinity College, Kandy, Ceylon
Enlisted in British Army at outbreak of World War I (University and Public School Brigade)
Took part in Battle of Mons
Took part in Battle of the Somme with 2nd Battalion, Royal Fusiliers; promoted to sergeant and wounded
Declined a commission and discharged from the Army at own request
Sent to India by the War Office
Took part in Third Afghan War
Served in North-West Frontier, Baluchistan, Waziristan and Peshawar
Promoted to acting major-general and given command of a division
Led a field force in the Annexation of Hyderabad, attacking from Vijayawada
Appointed General Officer Commanding, Southern Command
